history.change: measurement fix: the binary sniff tolerates a UTF-8 multibyte character cut at the 4096-byte sniff boundary; 1.0.0 misread a columned-LCTL unit longer than the sniff (its U+2502 separators) as binary and sent it to N_XLARGE as bulk instead of its own node

rules.rule: a script written in a node's own guest dialect goes to that node: MSSL assembly -> N_SMALL, LCTLC/1.1 -> N_MEDIUM, LCTLC/1.2 -> N_LARGE, LCTLC/1.0 (QVM profile) -> N_XLARGE
a PA-LCTL bundle (.pal) goes to N_MEDIUM, the reference node the corpora's own adapter binds
bulk cargo -- archives, images, binaries, media, PDFs, or anything >= 1 MiB -- goes to N_XLARGE, the roomiest, hosted node

hosted-runtime source (Python, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML/CSS/SVG, notebooks) and Columned LCTL plans (.lctl, verified by the JVM column verifier) go to N_XLARGE, the Python-hosted node with the JVM verifier
native/system source (C, C++, headers, assembly, Makefiles, linker scripts) goes to N_LARGE, the freestanding C core with the device I/O and service architecture
integrity and contract artifacts (sums, signatures, keys, manifests, schemas, provenance, ledgers, trust stores) go to N_MEDIUM, the node with signing, the trust chain and the independent verifier
structured data and configuration go by size: <= 4 KiB -> N_SMALL, <= 256 KiB -> N_MEDIUM, larger -> N_LARGE
launchers and shell/batch scripts go by complexity band: LOW -> N_SMALL, MID -> N_MEDIUM, HIGH -> N_LARGE, VERY_HIGH -> N_XLARGE
documents and notes go by size: <= 8 KiB -> N_SMALL (teaching), <= 128 KiB -> N_MEDIUM, larger -> N_LARGE
everything else goes by complexity band: LOW -> N_SMALL, MID -> N_MEDIUM, HIGH -> N_LARGE, VERY_HIGH -> N_XLARGE

portable_storage.rule: a script's identity is its original path; its bytes are stored under an alias only when that path cannot exist on every host (case collision, or a stored path over the budget); the ledger, CARGO.pal (stored=) and the cargo manifest record the alias

records.explanation: python needs a hosted runtime; the QUORUM node is Python-hosted with a JVM verifier
